releases.title: Rent-to-Own Industry Leaders Donate Over $81,000 in Furniture and Home Goods Following National Conference
releases.body:
12 RTO World 2026 Exhibitors Donated Showroom Items to Support Local Nonprofits

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following RTO World 2026, the national conference and trade show for the rent-to-own industry, 12 exhibitors donated more than $81,000 in furniture, mattresses, appliances, and home goods displayed during the event to nonprofit organizations serving youth and young adults in Palm Beach County, Florida. The Association of Professional Rental Organizations (APRO), the national trade association for the rent-to-own industry, coordinated the donations following the Aug. 24-27, 2026, conference in West Palm Beach.

The donated items went to Vita Nova, a Palm Beach County nonprofit that helps young adults ages 18 to 25 transition from homelessness or foster care to stable, independent living, and Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County, which provides safe, welcoming spaces and programs that help thousands of local children and teens learn, grow, and build skills for the future.

The effort was made possible in part through Aaron's, one of the largest rent-to-own operators and longtime APRO member, which helped connect APRO with Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County. Aaron's has a longstanding relationship with Boys & Girls Clubs across the country.

"RTO World brings together companies from across the rent-to-own industry, and we wanted to make sure that when we came to West Palm Beach, we left something meaningful behind," said Charles Smitherman, CEO of APRO. "Our member brands stepped up with furniture, mattresses, appliances, and other products they were happy to donate, and we were able to connect those resources with local organizations that could put them to good use. It's an incredible example of our industry coming together to make a positive impact in the communities that welcome us."

The following companies contributed items collected at RTO World 2026:

  • Almo – 3 washing machines, 3 dryers, 1 washer/dryer stack, 5 refrigerators, 2 freezers, and 1 range
  • Ashley Furniture – 4 sectionals, 2 loveseats, 1 sofa, 3 queen bedroom sets, 3 mattresses, 4 dining sets, 1 desk, 1 TV stand, lamps, tables, rugs, and metal foundations
  • CordaRoy's – 3 convertible bean bag beds
  • Corsicana – 4 queen mattresses and 5 bed frames
  • Global Furniture – 1 recliner, 1 sofa bed, 1 dining set, 2 sofas, 2 fireplace/speaker units, and 1 queen bedroom set
  • Jamison Bedding – 6 mattresses, including 3 queen and 3 twin
  • Living Essentials – 1 TV stand, 1 king bed and frame, 1 queen bed and mattress, 1 nightstand, 1 fireplace/TV stand, 1 banquette/fireplace, 1 lounger, 1 shelving/coffee table unit, and 1 recliner
  • Million Dollar Rustic – 1 fireplace, 1 farmhouse table, 4 stools, 1 pantry, and 1 nightstand
  • Nav-Air – 2 speakers
  • Simply Bunk Beds – 1 twin/twin loft bed, 1 twin/twin bunk bed with twin trundle, 1 twin captain's bed, all with mattresses
  • Southerland – 8 queen mattresses, 6 queen frames, and 2 twin frames
  • Tempur Sealy International – 11 queen mattresses, 9 queen platform bases, and 2 queen boxsprings with frames

"This generous furniture donation means so much to Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County and, most importantly, to the young people we serve," said Erin Nicoloso, Vice President of Marketing and Business Development for the Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County. "These pieces will help us create welcoming, comfortable, and inspiring spaces where our Club members can learn, connect, and grow. Donations like this allow us to invest more of our resources directly into the programs and opportunities our kids deserve, and we are incredibly grateful for this meaningful donation!"

"Many of the young adults we serve arrive with just the clothes on their back and are moving into a place that may be empty or without reliable appliances or bedding," said Gary Graham, Housing Supervisor of Vita Nova. "This donation helps them transition from the street to a house and turn that house into a home. It also means the thousands of dollars we would have spent finding mattresses, furniture, and appliances can instead go directly toward more leases, meals, and services that help get more young people off the streets."

In addition to its philanthropic efforts, APRO serves as a central resource for rent-to-own businesses seeking insights, education, and tools to strengthen operations and better serve consumers.

The U.S. rent-to-own industry generated approximately $11.8 billion in revenue in 2025, served more than 6.7 million households, and employed more than 34,000 Americans, according to APRO's 2026 Rent-to-Own Industry Health Survey.

APRO's work to strengthen the rent-to-own industry was recently recognized with a 2026 Power of Associations Silver Award from the American Society of Association Executives (ASAE) and the 2026 Association Impact Award from the Texas Society of Association Executives (TSAE). Both honors recognized APRO's Generative Knowledge Initiative, which works to improve the accuracy, accessibility, and authority of rent-to-own information available online.

To learn more about APRO, visit www.rtohq.org or follow the organization on Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn.

About APRO

The Association of Professional Rental Organizations (APRO), formerly Association of Progressive Rental Organizations, is the national trade association representing the rent-to-own (RTO) industry. Established in 1980 to advocate for and support the interests of RTO businesses, APRO provides its 330 member brands with essential resources, industry insights, and a strong community network. Through educational initiatives, legislative advocacy, and professional development opportunities, APRO strives to elevate the standards and success of the RTO sector, ensuring it continues to thrive and serve customers with integrity and excellence.

releases.title: Paralyzed Veterans of America Takes 2026 Healthcare Summit + Expo to Vegas to Advance Care for Spinal Cord Injury, MS, and ALS
releases.body:
VA Secretary Doug Collins plus 400+ clinicians across U.S. unite to discuss emerging research, evaluate new tech, share breakthroughs, and strengthen medical care

LAS VEGAS, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Paralyzed Veterans of America today officially commenced its 2026 Healthcare Summit + Expo at the Horseshoe Hotel in Las Vegas, bringing together more than 400 healthcare professionals from across the U.S. to explore emerging research, evaluate new technologies, share medical breakthroughs, and strengthen care for veterans and others living with spinal cord injuries, MS, and ALS. The event, which kicked off with a welcome reception on August 30 and concludes on September 2, features 110 speakers, 60 exhibitors, and remarks from Department of Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins.

"Healthcare doesn't start or end when veterans with traumatic spinal cord injuries and diseases, like MS and ALS, enter or leave the hospital - it begins well before injury or diagnosis… in research and at the lab, and it continues well afterwards when they return home, undergo rehab, and go on with life," said Robert Thomas, U.S. Army veteran and national president of Paralyzed Veterans of America. "PVA has spent 80 years bringing the right people together to solve complex problems and create greater possibilities for the veterans we serve. PVA's Healthcare Summit is a powerful example of that work. By connecting the people driving progress across SCI/D care, we help turn new ideas into better outcomes, which produce greater independence for patients in communities across the country."

Since PVA's founding in 1946, PVA has been a leading force in protecting, advancing, and strengthening specialized SCI/D care. The organization is the only nonprofit Veterans Service Organization granted access inside all 25 VA SCI/D Centers, giving PVA a direct view into the needs of catastrophically injured veterans, the realities facing their care teams, and the opportunities to consistently improve VA's system of care. That perspective has also informed PVA's investments in research, clinical education – like its annual Healthcare Summit, advocacy, and innovation.

"People living with spinal cord injuries, MS and ALS deserve care that keeps pace with the latest advances, and that starts with ensuring clinicians have opportunities to learn, collaborate, and grow," said Lindsay Perlman, director of PVA's Research and Education Department. "PVA's Healthcare Summit + Expo gives clinicians both inside the VA and out in the community space to do just that. Here they can step away from the demands of daily care, engage with likeminded professionals, and think differently about how they can better serve their patients."

Later in the week, on September 2, the Summit will honor six clinicians from across the nation with PVA's Clinical Excellence Awards, recognizing their exceptional dedication to caring for veterans and others living with SCI/D. This year's honorees are:

  • Marinella Galea, MD, Chief of Spinal Cord Injury and Disorders at the James J. Peters VA Medical Center in Bronx, New York, whose more than two decades of leadership advanced specialized SCI/D care, research, education, and patient safety;
  • Nicholas Wendel, PT, DPT, NCS, Physical Therapy Clinical Specialist at VA Boston Health Care System's West Roxbury VA in Massachusetts, recognized for using evidence-based rehabilitation and innovative technologies to help veterans increase mobility and independence;
  • Beth Whittington, MD, neurologist at the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center in Indianapolis, Indiana, whose work expanded access to specialized interdisciplinary ALS care through telehealth;
  • Ginger Willoughby, RN, BSN, MSN, CCM, Inpatient Nurse Care Coordinator at the Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center in Ohio, recognized for strengthening care coordination, quality improvement, caregiver education, and staff development;
  • Felicia Skelton, MD, MS, physician and faculty investigator at the Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center in Houston, Texas, whose research and innovative care models advanced SCI primary care, patient safety, and virtual access; and
  • Liam Kiernan, PT, DPT, NCS, OCS, Clinical Specialist Physical Therapist at the Rocky Mountain Regional VA Medical Center in Aurora, Colorado, recognized for bringing advanced rehabilitation technologies into clinical practice while contributing to research, education, and mentorship.

PVA is grateful for the generous support of this year's sponsors, including Biogen, First Nation Group, Genentech, Maxim Healthcare, NMEDA, Novartis, ONWARD Medical Inc., Permobil, Quantum, and Shionogi. Visit SummitPVA.org to learn more.

About Paralyzed Veterans of America

Paralyzed Veterans of America is a 501(c)(3) non-profit and the only congressionally chartered veterans service organization dedicated solely for the benefit and representation of veterans with spinal cord injury or diseases. The organization ensures veterans receive the benefits earned through service to our nation; monitors their care in VA spinal cord injury units; and funds research and education in the search for a cure and improved care for individuals with paralysis.

As a life-long partner and advocate for veterans and all people with disabilities, PVA also develops training and career services, works to ensure accessibility in public buildings and spaces, and provides health and rehabilitation opportunities through sports and recreation. With more than 70 offices and 33 chapters, Paralyzed Veterans of America serves veterans, their families, and their caregivers in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. Learn more at PVA.org.
